lessons.title: A Paris club is born
lessons.subtitle: A merger gave the capital a new team

story.title: A club wanted by Paris
story.body: With no Parisian side in the top division, a campaign for a major Paris club drew support from 66,000 people.

story.title: A merger made it possible
story.body: Paris Football Club joined with Stade Sangermanois. The merged club earned promotion in its first season.

facts.label: Public support
facts.prompt: How many people backed the project for a major Paris club?
facts.scope: The official PSG history reports this number for the public consultation before the club was created.
facts.evidence: The article says 66,000 people supported the project.

facts.label: Merger partner
facts.prompt: Which club merged with Paris Football Club to form PSG?
facts.scope: The club named in PSG’s official account of its 1970 formation.
facts.evidence: The article says PFC was forced to merge with Stade Sangermanois.

facts.label: First-season achievement
facts.prompt: What did PSG achieve in its first season?
facts.scope: The club’s first season after its 1970 creation.
facts.evidence: PSG records a National Championship title and promotion to the first division.

lessons.title: Brussels brings a European first
lessons.subtitle: N’Gotty’s strike made history

story.title: A final in Brussels
story.body: On 8 May 1996, PSG met Rapid Vienna in the Cup Winners’ Cup final at the Stade du Roi Baudouin.

story.title: One free kick decided it
story.body: Bruno N’Gotty struck from a long-range free kick before half-time. PSG held on for a 1–0 win and its first European trophy.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did PSG defeat in the 1996 Cup Winners’ Cup final?
facts.scope: The opponent in the 8 May 1996 final.
facts.evidence: The UEFA final report lists Paris Saint-Germain 1–0 SK Rapid Wien.

facts.label: Final scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored the only goal of the 1996 final?
facts.scope: PSG’s scorer in its 1–0 final win.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies N’Gotty as the scorer after a Djorkaeff touch from a free kick.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did PSG win the Cup Winners’ Cup in Brussels?
facts.scope: The date in PSG’s official final summary.
facts.evidence: PSG dates the Brussels final to Wednesday 8 May 1996.

lessons.title: Four past Barcelona
lessons.subtitle: A first-leg masterclass at the Parc

story.title: A fast start
story.body: On 14 February 2017, PSG overwhelmed Barcelona in the first leg of their Champions League round-of-16 tie.

story.title: Two from Di María
story.body: Ángel Di María scored twice; Julian Draxler and Edinson Cavani added one apiece in the 4–0 win.

facts.label: First-leg score
facts.prompt: What was the score when PSG hosted Barcelona on 14 February 2017?
facts.scope: The first leg of the 2016/17 Champions League round of 16 at the Parc des Princes.
facts.evidence: UEFA says PSG won 4–0.

facts.label: Two-goal scorer
facts.prompt: Which PSG player scored twice that night?
facts.scope: The PSG player with a brace in the 2017 first leg.
facts.evidence: UEFA names Di María as the two-goal scorer.

facts.label: Second scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored PSG’s second goal?
facts.scope: The player who made it 2–0 just before half-time.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes Verratti setting up Draxler’s finish.

lessons.title: A prodigy rises at Monaco
lessons.subtitle: A late-season surge helped deliver the league title

story.title: A first taste
story.body: Mbappé made his Ligue 1 debut for Monaco in December 2015. His first half-season brought 11 league appearances, one goal and one assist.

story.title: A decisive run
story.body: In 2016/17, the 17-year-old became central to Monaco’s title race. Across 13 closing matches, he scored 12 goals and assisted three, including the title-clinching goal on 17 May 2017.

facts.label: Ligue 1 debut
facts.prompt: In which month and year did Mbappé make his Ligue 1 debut?
facts.scope: Mbappé’s first Ligue 1 appearance for Monaco, in the 2015/16 season.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1’s retrospective says he discovered the league in December 2015.

facts.label: First half-season
facts.prompt: How many Ligue 1 goals did Mbappé score in his first half-season with Monaco?
facts.scope: His 11 Ligue 1 appearances in the first half of 2015/16.
facts.evidence: The league retrospective records 11 appearances, one goal and one assist in his first half-season.

facts.label: Title-clinching goal
facts.prompt: On what date did Mbappé score the goal that clinched Monaco’s 2016/17 league title?
facts.scope: The delayed league match against Saint-Étienne that secured Monaco’s 2016/17 Ligue 1 title.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 dates the title-clinching goal against ASSE to 17 May 2017.

lessons.title: A hat-trick at Camp Nou
lessons.subtitle: Mbappé turns the tie around

story.title: Paris responds
story.body: On 16 February 2021, Barcelona scored first at Camp Nou. Mbappé equalised before Paris took control.

story.title: Three goals away
story.body: Mbappé scored a treble in a 4–1 first-leg win. UEFA named him Player of the Match.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: When did Mbappé score his Camp Nou hat-trick?
facts.scope: The first leg of PSG’s Champions League round-of-16 tie.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the match Tuesday, 16 February 2021.

facts.label: Goals scored
facts.prompt: How many goals did Mbappé score against Barcelona in that match?
facts.scope: His total in PSG’s 4–1 win at Camp Nou.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Mbappé’s treble.

facts.label: UEFA match award
facts.prompt: What match award did UEFA give Mbappé after the Barcelona game?
facts.scope: UEFA’s designation for his performance in the 4–1 victory.
facts.evidence: The report lists Kylian Mbappé as Player of the Match.

lessons.title: Goal 201 makes history
lessons.subtitle: A personal milestone against Nantes

story.title: A record at the Parc
story.body: On 4 March 2023, Mbappé scored his 201st PSG goal against Nantes in a 4–2 league win.

story.title: The new leading scorer
story.body: At 24 years and 2 months, he passed Edinson Cavani’s club record, reaching the mark in 247 appearances.

facts.label: Record date
facts.prompt: When did Mbappé score his 201st PSG goal?
facts.scope: His record-breaking goal against Nantes.
facts.evidence: PSG dates the goal Saturday 4 March 2023.

facts.label: Appearances at milestone
facts.prompt: How many matches had Mbappé played for PSG when he reached 201 goals?
facts.scope: His appearances through the 4 March 2023 Nantes match.
facts.evidence: The PSG report states 201 goals in 247 matches.

facts.label: Age at milestone
facts.prompt: How old was Mbappé when he became PSG’s leading scorer?
facts.scope: Age reported by the club at the 201-goal milestone.
facts.evidence: PSG states his age as 24 years, 2 months and 12 days.

lessons.title: A record run of league honours
lessons.subtitle: Mbappé’s individual awards set new Ligue 1 marks

story.title: Five best-player awards
story.body: Ligue 1’s official honours list credits Mbappé with five Player of the Year awards: 2019 and four straight from 2021 through 2024.

story.title: Six scoring crowns
story.body: He became the first player to win the Ligue 1 top-scorer title six times, leading the league every season from 2019 through 2024. His PSG side also reached the 2020 Champions League final.

facts.label: Ligue 1 player award
facts.prompt: How many Ligue 1 Player of the Year awards does the league list for Mbappé?
facts.scope: Five awards listed through the 2023/24 season: 2019 and 2021–2024.
facts.evidence: The LFP honours list names Mbappé as winner in 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024.

facts.label: League top-scorer seasons
facts.prompt: How many consecutive Ligue 1 top-scorer titles did Mbappé win from 2019 to 2024?
facts.scope: Six consecutive seasonal titles from 2018/19 through 2023/24.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 calls him the first six-time top scorer and lists the six winning years 2019–2024.

facts.label: Champions League final
facts.prompt: In which year did Mbappé play the final PSG lost 1–0 to Bayern?
facts.scope: The Lisbon final in which Kingsley Coman scored for Bayern.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the Paris–Bayern final to August 2020.

lessons.title: Ibrahimović joins PSG
lessons.subtitle: A transfer from Milan began four seasons in Paris

story.title: From Milan to Paris
story.body: PSG signed Ibrahimović from AC Milan on 18 July 2012. UEFA reported that the striker agreed to a three-year contract.

story.title: His longest club stay
story.body: Paris became Ibrahimović’s longest spell at one club. Ligue 1 records 180 appearances for PSG in all competitions, more than he made for any other side.

facts.label: Signing date
facts.prompt: On what date did UEFA report Ibrahimović’s move from Milan to PSG?
facts.scope: The date UEFA reported PSG had signed the player from AC Milan.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s transfer report dates the agreement to 18 July 2012 and identifies AC Milan as his previous club.

facts.label: Contract length
facts.prompt: How long was the contract in UEFA’s signing report?
facts.scope: The contract length announced with the July 2012 transfer.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Ibrahimović agreed a three-year contract.

facts.label: PSG appearances
facts.prompt: How many total appearances did Ibrahimović make for PSG?
facts.scope: All-competition PSG appearances across his four-year spell.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1’s retrospective says 180 appearances, his highest total at any club.

lessons.title: An immediate impact in Paris
lessons.subtitle: Ibrahimović rescued PSG on his league debut

story.title: A debut brace
story.body: Ibrahimović’s first PSG league appearance came at the Parc des Princes on 11 August 2012 against Lorient. After PSG fell two goals behind, his first Ligue 1 brace brought them back level.

story.title: A four-year run
story.body: The comeback launched a four-season Paris stay. He went on to score 113 Ligue 1 goals in 122 appearances and lead the league in scoring three times.

facts.label: Lille match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Ibrahimović make his first Ligue 1 appearance for PSG?
facts.scope: His first PSG Ligue 1 appearance, at home against Lorient.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 dates his first Paris appearance to 11 August 2012 against FC Lorient.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did PSG face in Ibrahimović’s first league appearance?
facts.scope: The opponent in his PSG Ligue 1 debut on 11 August 2012.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 identifies FC Lorient as the opponent in his first PSG league appearance.

facts.label: Season milestone
facts.prompt: How many goals did PSG trail by before Ibrahimović’s debut brace rescued a draw?
facts.scope: The score deficit overcome in the 11 August 2012 league match against Lorient.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 says his brace rescued PSG after the team fell two goals behind.

lessons.title: A historic scoring season
lessons.subtitle: His final Ligue 1 campaign set a personal peak

story.title: Thirty-eight goals
story.body: In 2015/16 Ibrahimović scored 38 Ligue 1 goals in 31 appearances. It was the league’s third-highest single-season total at the time.

story.title: A rare four-goal match
story.body: On 13 March 2016, he scored four times in PSG’s 9–0 win at Troyes, as the club secured the title with eight league matches remaining.

facts.label: League goals
facts.prompt: How many Ligue 1 goals did Ibrahimović score in the 2015/16 season?
facts.scope: His 2015/16 Ligue 1 season total, scored in 31 appearances.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 records 38 goals in 31 matches for 2015/16.

facts.label: League assists
facts.prompt: What place did his 38-goal 2015/16 total hold in Ligue 1 single-season history?
facts.scope: Historical league ranking cited by Ligue 1 for his 2015/16 tally.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1 describes 38 goals as the third-highest total in the championship’s history.

facts.label: Troyes goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Ibrahimović score in PSG’s 9–0 win at Troyes?
facts.scope: PSG’s Ligue 1 away win at Troyes on 13 March 2016.
facts.evidence: Ligue 1’s season retrospective calls the four-goal performance a quadruple.

lessons.title: A final match with a brace
lessons.subtitle: Ibrahimović signed off with a Coupe de France win

story.title: A cup final farewell
story.body: Ibrahimović’s final PSG match was the Coupe de France final on 21 May 2016 against Marseille. PSG won 4–2 at the Stade de France.

story.title: A decisive finish
story.body: The Swedish striker scored twice in the final. The victory gave PSG its tenth Coupe de France, matching Marseille’s tally at the time.

facts.label: Final match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Ibrahimović score twice in PSG’s Coupe de France final against Marseille?
facts.scope: The 2016 Coupe de France final, which was Ibrahimović’s last PSG match.
facts.evidence: The FFF archive dates the final to 21 May 2016 and identifies it as PSG–Marseille.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did PSG beat in Ibrahimović’s final match?
facts.scope: The opponent in the 2016 Coupe de France final.
facts.evidence: The FFF archive identifies Olympique de Marseille as the opponent.

facts.label: Career total
facts.prompt: How many goals did Ibrahimović score in the final?
facts.scope: His scoring total in the 21 May 2016 Coupe de France final.
facts.evidence: The FFF final archive says Ibrahimović scored a brace in PSG’s 4–2 win.

lessons.title: From St Mark’s to Manchester City
lessons.subtitle: A church team evolved into a city club

story.title: A local beginning
story.body: St Mark’s Church formed a football team in 1880. That team would eventually become Manchester City.

story.title: A name for the whole city
story.body: The team became Ardwick in 1887, then reorganised as Manchester City Football Club in 1894.

facts.label: Founding church
facts.prompt: Which church formed the team that evolved into Manchester City?
facts.scope: Manchester City’s origins in West Gorton, 1880.
facts.evidence: City’s club-history timeline identifies St Mark’s Church as the origin of the team.

facts.label: Ardwick year
facts.prompt: In what year did St Mark’s evolve into Ardwick AFC?
facts.scope: The name and ground move listed in the official timeline.
facts.evidence: The history says the team became Ardwick AFC in 1887.

facts.label: Manchester City name
facts.prompt: In what year did Ardwick reform as Manchester City Football Club?
facts.scope: The club’s reorganisation to represent the whole city.
facts.evidence: Manchester City dates this change to 1894.

lessons.title: A trophy after 35 years
lessons.subtitle: Yaya Touré’s Wembley goal ends the wait

story.title: A Wembley final
story.body: On 14 May 2011, City faced Stoke in the FA Cup final, looking to end a 35-year wait for a major trophy.

story.title: One strike settled it
story.body: Yaya Touré scored in the 74th minute for a 1–0 win. The cup began a new successful period for the club.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: When did City beat Stoke in the 2011 FA Cup final?
facts.scope: The Wembley final that ended City’s 35-year wait for a major trophy.
facts.evidence: The official club retrospective lists 14 May 2011.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score against Stoke in the FA Cup final?
facts.scope: The result that gave City the cup.
facts.evidence: Manchester City records a 1–0 win over Stoke.

facts.label: Final scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored the only goal in the final?
facts.scope: The scorer of the 74th-minute goal.
facts.evidence: The club says Touré scored the winner 16 minutes from time.

lessons.title: City completes the Treble
lessons.subtitle: Rodri’s strike brings a first Champions League

story.title: A first European Cup
story.body: On 10 June 2023, City faced Inter in Istanbul in its first Champions League final.

story.title: One goal was enough
story.body: Rodri scored in the second half for a 1–0 win. City completed the Treble with its first Champions League crown.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: When did City beat Inter to win its first Champions League?
facts.scope: The final in Istanbul.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the final Saturday 10 June 2023.

facts.label: Final scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored the only goal against Inter?
facts.scope: The scorer in the 1–0 Champions League final.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies Rodri as the second-half scorer.

facts.label: Achievement
facts.prompt: What major English football achievement did City complete with the win?
facts.scope: City’s league, FA Cup and Champions League success in 2022/23.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes the Champions League win as completing a treble.

lessons.title: Agüero joins City
lessons.subtitle: An immediate impact from his debut

story.title: A new signing
story.body: Agüero joined Manchester City on 27 July 2011 after five seasons at Atlético Madrid.

story.title: A fast introduction
story.body: He made his City debut against Swansea on 15 August and scored 30 times in his first season.

facts.label: Signing date
facts.prompt: On what date did Agüero join Manchester City?
facts.scope: His joining date in the club’s official biography.
facts.evidence: The City profile says he joined on 27 July 2011.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Agüero face on his City debut?
facts.scope: The Etihad match on 15 August 2011.
facts.evidence: City identifies Swansea as his debut opponent.

facts.label: First-season goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Agüero score in his first City season?
facts.scope: His 2011/12 first season at City.
facts.evidence: The club biography says he scored 30 times.

lessons.title: The 93:20 winner
lessons.subtitle: Agüero turns a title race around

story.title: A late comeback
story.body: On 13 May 2012, QPR led City 2–1 late in stoppage time while City needed a win to be champions.

story.title: A decisive finish
story.body: Agüero scored at 93:20 to make it 3–2 and secure City’s first Premier League title.

facts.label: Title-winning date
facts.prompt: On what date did Agüero score the 93:20 goal?
facts.scope: The final day of the 2011/12 Premier League season.
facts.evidence: City identifies the QPR win as the last day of the 2011/12 campaign.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when City beat QPR with Agüero’s goal?
facts.scope: The comeback victory at the Etihad.
facts.evidence: City’s retrospective describes the 3–2 win after City had trailed 2–1.

facts.label: Goal time
facts.prompt: At what time did Agüero score the title-winning goal?
facts.scope: The match clock for the famous goal.
facts.evidence: City and the Premier League refer to the goal as 93:20.

lessons.title: A record City goalscorer
lessons.subtitle: His 260 goals came in 390 games

story.title: An all-time club record
story.body: Agüero finished his City career with 260 goals in 390 appearances, the club record at the time of his departure.

story.title: A Premier League mark
story.body: He also set the league record for most hat-tricks, with 12, across his City seasons.

facts.label: City goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Agüero score for City?
facts.scope: His final club total in the City legend profile.
facts.evidence: Manchester City records 260 goals.

facts.label: City appearances
facts.prompt: How many City appearances did Agüero make?
facts.scope: His total for the club across 2011–2021.
facts.evidence: The City profile lists 390 appearances.

facts.label: Premier League hat-tricks
facts.prompt: How many Premier League hat-tricks did Agüero score, a league record?
facts.scope: His Premier League career total in the competition’s record table.
facts.evidence: The Premier League record list identifies Agüero with 12.

lessons.title: A medal-winning City era
lessons.subtitle: Five league titles among his honours

story.title: A decorated spell
story.body: City lists 14 medals for Agüero: five Premier League titles, five League Cups, one FA Cup and three Community Shields.

story.title: More than a goal
story.body: The honours came during a decade in which Agüero became the club’s leading scorer and an emblem of its rise.

facts.label: League titles
facts.prompt: How many Premier League titles did Agüero win with City?
facts.scope: The medal count in his official club profile.
facts.evidence: City lists five Premier League medals.

facts.label: League Cups
facts.prompt: How many League Cup medals does City list for Agüero?
facts.scope: The honours tally on the official biography.
facts.evidence: City lists five Carabao Cup medals.

facts.label: Total medals
facts.prompt: How many total medals does the City profile list for Agüero?
facts.scope: The total across his City honours in the club biography.
facts.evidence: City says he has 14 medals.

lessons.title: A World Cup winner arrives
lessons.subtitle: Silva joins from Valencia in 2010

story.title: From Gran Canaria
story.body: David Silva was born in Arguineguín, Gran Canaria, on 8 January 1986.

story.title: A summer move
story.body: A World Cup winner with Spain, he moved from Valencia to Manchester City in July 2010.

facts.label: Birthplace
facts.prompt: Where was David Silva born?
facts.scope: The birthplace given in Manchester City’s official profile.
facts.evidence: City says Silva was born in Arguineguín, Gran Canaria.

facts.label: City arrival year
facts.prompt: In which year did Silva arrive at Manchester City?
facts.scope: His transfer from Valencia to City.
facts.evidence: The club biography places his arrival in July 2010.

facts.label: Previous club
facts.prompt: Which club did Silva join City from?
facts.scope: The Spanish club he left before joining City.
facts.evidence: The official profile says he arrived from Valencia.

lessons.title: A derby remembered in passes
lessons.subtitle: Silva assists Džeko in the 6–1 win

story.title: Old Trafford, October 2011
story.body: City beat Manchester United 6–1 away in a landmark Premier League derby.

story.title: A creator’s contribution
story.body: The club later singled out Silva’s vision and execution in his assist for Edin Džeko as an example of his playmaking.

facts.label: Derby year
facts.prompt: In what year did City win 6–1 at Old Trafford with Silva assisting Džeko?
facts.scope: The away derby highlighted in City’s Silva tribute.
facts.evidence: City’s article describes the 6–1 defeat of United in 2011.

facts.label: Derby score
facts.prompt: What was the score when David Silva’s Manchester City won at Old Trafford on 23 October 2011?
facts.scope: The Premier League derby result.
facts.evidence: The club tribute calls it the 6–1 defeat of arch-rivals United.

facts.label: Assist recipient
facts.prompt: Who received Silva’s notable pass for a goal in that derby?
facts.scope: The City player whose goal followed Silva’s pass.
facts.evidence: City’s retrospective names Silva’s assist to Edin Džeko.

lessons.title: A decade of City appearances
lessons.subtitle: 436 games and a European milestone

story.title: A top-ten career
story.body: Silva’s 436th City appearance, against Lyon, moved him into the club’s all-time top ten in August 2020.

story.title: A European high
story.body: That Lyon match was his 70th European appearance for City, then a club record.

facts.label: City appearances
facts.prompt: How many appearances did Silva make for Manchester City?
facts.scope: His all-competitions total at the end of his City spell.
facts.evidence: City lists 436 appearances.

facts.label: European appearances
facts.prompt: How many European appearances did Silva have after the Lyon match?
facts.scope: His tally in European matches for City after facing Lyon.
facts.evidence: City says the Lyon fixture took him to 70 European appearances.

facts.label: City goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Silva score for City?
facts.scope: His total for Manchester City in the club profile.
facts.evidence: The official profile gives 77 goals.

lessons.title: Honours across a decade
lessons.subtitle: Four Premier League titles and more

story.title: A long list of silverware
story.body: Across ten years, Silva won four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups with City.

story.title: A lasting tribute
story.body: The club announced a statue and a training pitch mosaic to honour his contribution.

facts.label: Premier League titles
facts.prompt: How many Premier League titles did Silva win with City?
facts.scope: The title count in City’s honours announcement.
facts.evidence: City lists four Premier League titles.

facts.label: FA Cups
facts.prompt: How many FA Cups did Silva win with City?
facts.scope: His club honours across the decade.
facts.evidence: City lists two FA Cups.

facts.label: League Cups
facts.prompt: How many League Cups did Silva win with City?
facts.scope: The club’s honours count.
facts.evidence: City lists five League Cups.

lessons.title: Athletic Club de Madrid begins
lessons.subtitle: Students start a club in 1903

story.title: A group of students
story.body: Young Basque students living in Madrid founded Athletic Club de Madrid on 26 April 1903.

story.title: A pitch by the Retiro
story.body: The club’s first field stood behind the Retiro walls; members played the first match on 2 May.

facts.label: Foundation date
facts.prompt: On what date was Athletic Club de Madrid founded?
facts.scope: The official foundation date stated by Atlético.
facts.evidence: The club’s anniversary article identifies 26 April 1903.

facts.label: Founders
facts.prompt: Who founded Athletic Club de Madrid?
answers: Young Basque students living in Madrid

value.display: Young Basque students living in Madrid
value.text: Young Basque students living in Madrid

facts.scope: The people identified in the official anniversary account.
facts.evidence: Atlético describes the founders as young Basque students based in Madrid.

facts.label: First match
facts.prompt: When did members play the club’s first match?
facts.scope: The members’ first club match, played at Campo del Retiro on 2 May 1903.
facts.evidence: The club’s official first-match retrospective says the first game took place on 2 May 1903 at Campo del Retiro.

lessons.title: A title secured at Camp Nou
lessons.subtitle: Godín’s header earns the point

story.title: A final-day decider
story.body: On 17 May 2014, Atlético visited Barcelona knowing a draw would secure the league title.

story.title: A header after the break
story.body: Diego Godín rose to meet Koke’s corner. The 1–1 draw gave Atlético its tenth Spanish league championship.

facts.label: Title date
facts.prompt: When did Atlético secure the 2013/14 league title at Barcelona?
facts.scope: The final league match of the title-winning season.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the match Saturday 17 May 2014.

facts.label: Equaliser scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Atlético’s equaliser at Camp Nou?
facts.scope: The header that made the score 1–1.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies Godín as the second-half scorer.

facts.label: League title number
